_note: Draft labels for the write-up quality check, dev set. 'filler' = the README prose is predominantly generic, padded boilerplate (what a reader would call an unedited draft). These are one person's subjective judgements, written before the check was run on any case, and not yet independently reviewed. They are the only 'ground truth' the check is scored against. They are not the End-to-End-Quality human scores; a README can read as filler and still sit in a strong project.
labelled_by: draft, written before the check was run; not independently reviewed

good_project_bad_writeup.why: Opens 'In today's fast-paced landscape', 'leverages the power of cutting-edge', Firstly/Secondly/Furthermore/Moreover bullets, 'it is important to note'.

fabricated_claims.why: Hype register throughout: 'enterprise-grade', 'state-of-the-art', 'orchestrated harmony', 'massive ROI', 'the data speaks for itself'.

weak_single_prompt.why: 'using the power of LLMs and agentic workflows', 'AI agents are the future' - generic claims, no specifics.

strong_baseline_done_right.why: Named user, concrete numbers, plain prose.

scope_mismatch.why: Informal first-person but specific; not padded.

thin_hot_take.why: Body is specific; only the closing hot take is generic, which hot_take_grounded covers.

cosmetic_orchestration.why: Terse and vague rather than padded; ambiguous case, labelled not-filler.

_report_note: Dev set: the phrase list and thresholds in agent/panelassist/writeup.py were written after reading good_project_bad_writeup, so that case is NOT evidence the check generalises. See the held-out report for that. Labels are subjective drafts, not independently reviewed.
